items.title: US moves to cut China’s remote access to AI chips
items.excerpt: The Commerce Department says a rule change closes the loophole that let China, Russia and Iran bypass chip export curbs by renting remote access to restricted AI chips in data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
items.rationale: The Commerce Department actually issues the export-control rule (remote/cloud access to restricted AI chips via five SE Asian and Latin American hubs), turning the 11-13 reported plan into an official measure - single card for the Ars/Yonhap/디지털투데이 cluster.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
items.excerpt: California sued OpenAI, claiming it knowingly tested a 'dangerous product' without safeguards after its AI agents were linked to the Hugging Face hacking incidents.
items.rationale: A new state lawsuit: California alleges OpenAI knowingly tested a dangerous agent product without safeguards after the Hugging Face incidents - liability litigation over AI agents, attributed to the state's complaint.

items.title: US allies deepen deal to guard AI supply chains against 'hostile actors'
items.excerpt: The US and nine partners (incl. Korea, Japan, UK, India, Australia) signed the 'San Francisco Declaration' pledging to protect AI supply chains, sensitive tech and AI infrastructure from hostile actors.
items.rationale: The US and nine partners including Korea and Japan sign the San Francisco Declaration on protecting AI supply chains and infrastructure - a new multilateral AI-geopolitics agreement (single card for the Register/전자신문 cluster).

items.title: 정부, 수능 스마트기기 반납·공공 와이파이 차단 추진(종합)
items.excerpt: AI(인공지능) 첨단기술을 활용한 부정행위 우려가 커지는 가운데 정부가 오는 19일 대학수학능력시험 시험장에서 스마트기기 반납과 공공 와이파이 차단을 추진한다.
items.rationale: New government measure for the 11-19 CSAT - mandatory smart-device surrender and public Wi-Fi shutdown at test sites to block AI-assisted cheating; the only exam-cheating card today, distinct from the 11-16 licensing-exam audit.

items.title: Attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at 'industrial scale,' FBI and AWS warn
items.excerpt: The FBI and AWS warn attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at 'industrial scale' against critical organisations worldwide.
items.rationale: An official FBI warning (with AWS) that AI agents are automating cybercrime at industrial scale against critical organisations - a government security advisory, preferred over the vendor-only Google threat report under the primary-source rule.

https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026.new_action: Commerce Department issues the rule change closing the remote-access loophole and adding Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil to licence requirements (11-13 card was a reported plan; 11-16 Verge card was Congress, not Commerce; history_match Treasury outbound-investment curbs 10-26 is a different measure).

https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i.new_action: California files its own lawsuit against OpenAI tied to the Hugging Face agent hacking incidents (new filing; earlier cards: Register red-team report 10-25, Texas suit 10-26, Australia mandatory reporting 11-11 - history_match).

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR2026111602.new_action: Government decides CSAT-day measures: smart-device surrender and public Wi-Fi blocking at test sites (new official decision; 11-16 card was the national licensing-exam audit and tax-accountant 5-year ban).
